newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West spot power weaker amid warmer weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West spot power weaker amid warmer weather.

text.p: Spot power prices in the U.S. West fell further Friday amid warmer weather in the Northwest and the approach of slower weekend demand.
"There are a lot more sellers than buyers. Prices are coming down quickly," said one Northwest trader.
Market sources expected the downtrend to continue next week, when hydroelectric dam flow restrictions related to fish spawning are scheduled to end.
In addition, a 700 megawatt (MW) unit at the Colstrip coal-fired power plant in Montana is scheduled to restart on Saturday after being down for a week of unplanned repair work.
Sources also noted, however, that the 1,070 MW unit 2 at the San Onofre nuclear power plant in California is scheduled to shut November 30 for a 70-day refueling outage.

Firm, on-peak power for Monday at the California-Oregon border (COB) was last quoted $27.00-28.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), down from $29.50-30.50 on Thursday. Off-peak COB was quoted $15.50-16.50, down from $17.50-18.50.
Next-day firm, on-peak power at Mid-Columbia was quoted quoted $26.00-27.50, while off-peak was quoted $17.00-18.00.
Palo Verde next-day firm, on-peak power was quoted $24.50-25.50 per MWh, down from $26.00-28.00. Off-peak Palo Verde was quoted $13.00-14.50.
Four Corners firm, on-peak power was little changed at $25.00-27.00, while off-peak was at $14.00-16.00.
